label: early original-phase steps (t=2-4) after the sequence starts with s
explanation: Fires during the original (input) phase, 2-4 steps after an s that was among the first two tokens. When the sequence starts with s it fires at t=2..4; when s is the second token it fires at t=3..4. 99% of the activation mass is in the original phase and it peaks at t=3. When the first token is s, the rate is 18.6x baseline and that case holds 86% of the mass. The largest activations (about 4.1) come from sequences starting s s, at t=3, whatever the input token is. s as the second token gives weaker activations (mostly the second quartile). It does not fire at t=0 or 1, almost never at t>=6 or in the delimiter/copy phases, and barely at all without an early s. The rest of the activity (about 3% of mass) is tiny scattered activations at t=2-3. False positives are mostly s-second sequences at t=3-4 where it stays silent. Dev: P 0.86, R 0.82, F1 0.84, mass recall 0.97.

issues: Most of the factual claims hold. On the dev split, 99.1% of the activation mass is in the original phase. There are no activations at t=0 or t=1, the peak is at t=3 (50% of mass), and only 58 activations occur at t=6 and 1 at t=7. The delimiter phase holds 0.7% of mass and the copy phase 0.2%. The s-first clause alone scores precision 0.99 with mass recall 0.84 on test. Sequences starting 's s' at t=3 have precision 1.0.

Systematic false positives in the s-second clause. On test, with orig(1)==s, orig(0)!=s and t in 3..4, precision is only 0.67. These false positives are not scattered: whether the feature fires depends strongly on the first token. Dev precision by orig(0): b 1.00, d 0.99, t 0.99, w 0.99, f/i/n/v 0.98, but e 0.06, h 0.01, o 0.00, '2' 0.00, '3' 0.04, and roughly 0.4-0.5 for c, g, k, q and '0'. The third token makes no difference (precision 0.65-0.70 for every orig(2) tested).

The explanation says false positives are 's-second sequences at t=3-4 where the feature stays silent' but does not say they are predictable from the first token. That class accounts for most of the 10,176 test false positives.

Minor: the predicate is right to leave out t=5 for s-first sequences (precision 0.17) and the delimiter phase (precision 0.002). The missed activations are tiny and scattered, for example b-first at t=2 (precision 0.14, mass 0.2%). That part of the explanation is accurate.

The label 'after the sequence starts with s' undersells the s-second clause, which holds about 13% of mass and is not 'starts with s'. It also does not mention that the s-second case is gated by the first token.
skeptic.revised_label: early original-phase steps (t=2-4) after an s at position 0, or t=3-4 after an s at position 1 unless the first token is e, h, o, 2 or 3 (weaker for c, g, k, q, 0)
